tldr_label: TL;DR: COP31 collapses without a deal for the first time since 2009, a Russian strike levels a Dymer apartment block, and futures rebound as Asia moves to prop

tldr_bullets.label: Climate
tldr_bullets.body: The EU, UK, Norway, Panama and island states rejected a final COP31 text that did not mention fossil fuels. The summit ended without a decision after the longest overrun on record. [[TAG:danger:collapse]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: A Russian drone strike on an apartment block in Dymer, Kyiv region, killed at least 11. Zelensky urged the US to release Patriot interceptors. [[TAG:danger:civilians]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: US stock futures rose 2% to 3% on Sunday evening after the worst week since 2020 for the Nasdaq 100. South Korea, China and Taiwan announced market-support steps. [[TAG:info:rebound]]

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Trump urged Nvidia's board to rehire Jensen Huang, while Bessent said the government needs answers on chips reaching China. [[TAG:warning:board resists]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Four hours of Likud-Yashar coalition talks ended without agreement. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

sections.title: COP31: Collapse
sections.summary: EU-led bloc rejects text silent on fossil fuels; first COP without a deal since 2009

paragraphs.heading: No Agreement
paragraphs.body: CBS News and Al-Monitor, carrying Reuters, reported that COP31 ended Sunday without an agreement after the EU and others rejected the final text proposed by Turkey and Australia. RTE and CBC reported the text failed to mention fossil fuels. Yahoo, carrying AFP, called it the first such failure since 2009, and Newsbeep listed the UK, Norway, Panama and island states among those rejecting it. [[TAG:danger:no deal]]

paragraphs.heading: Blame and Aftermath
paragraphs.body: Business Standard reported a different account in which the EU, Russia and Arab states derailed the talks over fuel and climate finance. Developing-country officials accused the EU of backing away from finance commitments. Forbes said Turkey's grid and storage agenda now falls to utilities and lenders. Reuters-based reports said earlier COP commitments remain in force. [[TAG:warning:competing accounts]]

sections.sources: CBS News, Al-Monitor, RTE, CBC, Yahoo, Newsbeep, Business Standard, Forbes

sections.title: Ukraine: Dymer and the Deadline
sections.summary: Drone strike on Dymer apartment block kills 11; FT says US wants a deal by January

paragraphs.heading: Dymer
paragraphs.body: Ukrinform reported the death toll from a Russian strike on an apartment block in Dymer, Kyiv region, rose to 11. Kyiv Post put weekend deaths in the region at 15, and Latin Times reported up to 15 residents missing. Al Jazeera reported that Zelensky urged the US to release Patriot missiles. Kyiv Post reported Zelensky saying Russia launched 2,700 drones and 165 missiles in the past week. [[TAG:danger:Kyiv region]]

paragraphs.heading: January Push
paragraphs.body: Kyiv Post, TVP World and the Jerusalem Post, citing the Financial Times, reported that the Trump administration wants a Ukraine-Russia peace deal by early January, before Democrats take control of Congress. The report relies on anonymous sources, and European officials worried it would require major Ukrainian concessions. There has been no official confirmation of the deadline. [[TAG:warning:unconfirmed]]

sections.title: NATO: Poland's Ask
sections.summary: Warsaw seeks more Eastern Sentry assets as allies meet Monday

paragraphs.heading: The Request
paragraphs.body: United24 reported that Poland requested extra NATO forces under the Eastern Sentry mission after the airspace violation. Latin Times reported Warsaw is seeking more air-defense support but stopped short of formally triggering Article 4. Rapporteur reported Poland will receive strong support from allies. [[TAG:info:Eastern Sentry]]

paragraphs.heading: Background
paragraphs.body: NATO launched Eastern Sentry in September 2025, after Poland requested Article 4 consultations over Russian drones. Al Jazeera reported that analysts see direct confrontation with Russia as unlikely. Allied talks on Poland's proposals are expected Monday. [[TAG:warning:Monday]]

sections.title: Markets: Bounce and Backstops
sections.summary: US futures rebound 2% to 3%; Seoul, Beijing and Taipei roll out market supports

paragraphs.heading: Futures Rebound
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Nasdaq 100 futures rose about 3% as trading opened Sunday evening, kicking off a holiday-shortened week after the tech rout. Yahoo Finance reported Nvidia futures up about 6% and S&P 500 futures up about 2%, though figures varied by source and time. Investing.com reported Bessent's comments on the Nvidia probe as a market driver. [[TAG:success:rebound]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia Steps In
paragraphs.body: CNBC and Investing.com reported that South Korea announced emergency measures including preparations for a market support fund, China's exchanges eased margin financing rules, and Taiwan tightened short-selling rules. CNBC reported Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5% early Monday. Longbridge reported Tokyo was closed for a holiday. ABC Australia reported that the ASX also fell. [[TAG:warning:intervention]]

sections.title: Nvidia: The Huang Question
sections.summary: Trump urges board to rehire Huang; Bessent wants answers on chips to China

paragraphs.heading: Trump's Plea
paragraphs.body: The National and IBTimes reported that Trump called on Nvidia's board to rehire Jensen Huang, calling it the best thing for the USA. The board has said it will not reinstate him. [[TAG:warning:board resists]]

paragraphs.heading: Bessent
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Bessent said the government needs answers on Nvidia's role in AI chips reaching China, and described the Alice Huang allegations as kind of a canard. TheWrap and NewsNation also covered his remarks. Commentators differ on whether he opened the door to Huang's return; he did not explicitly endorse it. [[TAG:info:mixed signals]]

sections.title: Gulf: Attacks Up, Oil Down
sections.summary: Hormuz attacks hit wartime high and flows fall 15%, yet Brent slides on surplus

paragraphs.heading: Escalation
paragraphs.body: Yahoo reported that Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are at their highest level since the conflict began, and Al Jazeera examined what is behind the escalation. ABC News reported that Tehran said the strait will be safe if its demands are met. Many specific attack claims come from the IRGC and remain unverified. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

paragraphs.heading: The Oil Paradox
paragraphs.body: AGBI reported that Hormuz shipments dropped as attacks increased, citing Vortexa estimates of a roughly 15% fall to about 10.2 million barrels a day. Oilprice.com and Oil and Gas Middle East reported that Brent nonetheless fell for a third week as returning Gulf barrels and surplus forecasts weighed on prices. Flow estimates vary by source. [[TAG:info:surplus]]

paragraphs.heading: Coalition

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that displaced Palestinians protested as Israeli air strikes continued in Gaza. UN News reported that winter rains are deepening the crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts. [[TAG:danger:humanitarian]]
